$comment: One case per playground configuration. `why` writes out the arithmetic a reader would check, exactly as data/golden/vectors.json does for the evaluation engine: a bare expected number is a value somebody typed, and recomputing it in the test from the same annotation would mirror the implementation and prove nothing. content_lint.mjs refuses a case whose why is missing.

cases.why: ph-001 carries 6 objects and 6 annotated edges. Ordered pairs of distinct objects = 6 x 5 = 30. With the slice's 16 predicates the candidate space is 30 x 16 = 480. The annotated share is 6 / 480 = 0.0125.

Same 30 ordered pairs, but with VG-150's 50 predicates: 30 x 50 = 1500. The annotated share is 6 / 1500 = 0.004. This is the vocabulary M0's own worked example computes with, which is why it is offered.

Half of 6 edges is 3. The candidate space does not depend on how many edges were annotated, so it stays 480 and only the numerator moves: 3 / 480 = 0.00625. That the bound does not move is the point of the slider.
No edges kept. 0 / 480 = 0, which is zero and not undefined: the candidate space is non-empty, so the share is a real number.
6 objects give 6 x 5 = 30 ordered pairs of distinct objects, times 16 predicates = 480.
Discarding direction identifies (s,o) with (o,s), so 30 ordered pairs become 15 unordered ones: 15 x 16 = 240, exactly half of 480.
ph-001 relationship 1 is object 3 (box) --on--> object 1 (table). Unswapped, the triplet is the one the annotator wrote, so it is in E.
Swapped, the triplet is table --on--> box. No relationship in ph-001 has subject 1, object 3 and predicate on, so it is not in E. Not in E is not the same claim as false.

ph-001 relationship 2 is object 2 (person) --near--> object 1 (table). `near` reads as symmetric, but the annotator wrote one direction only, so table --near--> person is not in E. This is the case worth showing: the absence is a fact about the annotation, not about the world.

The 80 frames carry 36 predicates. Merging on, above, over and sitting on turns four classes into one: 36 - 4 + 1 = 33. Their distinct triplets are 248 + 11 + 5 + 10 = 274, and two pairs carry two members each, which E prime records once: 274 - 2 = 272.
Unmerged, the slice uses 36 predicates, and on alone carries 248 of the 684 distinct triplets (382 of the 892 annotation rows; E is a set). The other three members keep their own 11, 5 and 10.
The slice uses 115 object names. Merging man, person and people turns three into one: 115 - 3 + 1 = 113, with 56 + 52 + 19 = 127 objects in the merged class.
Frame 228, relationship 5 is glass (10) sitting on table (2). The frame carries no on edge from 10 to 2, so glass on table is not in E before the merge.
With on and sitting on merged, glass (10) sitting on table (2) and glass on table share the key (10, on, 2), so the substituted triplet is in E prime. No annotation and no model changed.
At s = 0 every class holds the same count, so the three most frequent of 36 hold 3 / 36 = 1/12 = 0.083333, and the rarest is as frequent as the first: 36^0 = 1.
H_4 at s = 1 is 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 = 25/12. The first class holds 1 / (25/12) = 12/25 = 0.48. The fourth is 4^(-1) = 0.25 of the first.
Counting distinct triplets, the slice's three most frequent predicates are on 248, near 54 and has 51: 248 + 54 + 51 = 353 of 684 triplets, and 353 / 684 = 0.516082.
v2 states 68,538 training images and the canonical protocol 57,723: 68,538 - 57,723 = 10,815, which is the card's own count of v2 training images kept with no relation.
v2 states 31,876 test images and the canonical protocol 26,446: 31,876 - 26,446 = 5,430, the card's count of v2 test images kept with no relation.
Issue 94 gives v1 73,538 training images against v2's 68,538: 73,538 - 68,538 = 5,000, the canonical validation set the card says v1 folded into train.
v1 has 27,032 test images and v2 31,876: 27,032 - 31,876 = -4,844. The 4,844 are the images the card says v1 took from the test pool for its validation set.
Xu et al. state 70% of 108,077 images and no count, so there is no count to subtract from 57,723. Multiplying 0.7 by 108,077 would assert a split size the paper never states.
Object 3 of ph-001 is 90 x 70 at (250, 240), A = 6300. At lambda 1 with no shift the prediction is the same box: intersection 6300, union 6300 + 6300 - 6300 = 6300, IoU = 6300 / 6300 = 1.

At lambda 1.4 the prediction is round(1.4 x 90) x round(1.4 x 70) = 126 x 98 = 12348, centred at (295, 275): x 232 to 358, y 226 to 324, containing the annotation. IoU = 6300 / 12348 = 0.510, which meets tau = 0.5; the bound 6300 / 12348 is the same number.

At lambda 1.5 the prediction is 135 x 105 = 14175 and contains the annotation, so IoU = 6300 / 14175 = 0.444. The bound 6300 / 14175 = 0.444 is below tau = 0.5, so no shift reaches tau: lambda is past sqrt(2).

Shifted 18 px right the prediction spans x 268 to 358. The overlap is (340 - 268) x 70 = 5040 and the union 6300 + 6300 - 5040 = 7560, so IoU = 5040 / 7560 = 0.667. Both areas are 6300, so the bound is 6300 / 6300 = 1.

Object 3 is 90 x 70 at (250, 240), A = 6300. Shifted 30 px right it spans x 280 to 370, so the overlap is (340 - 280) x 70 = 4200 and the union is 6300 + 6300 - 4200 = 8400. IoU = 4200 / 8400 = 0.5, which meets tau = 0.5 because acceptance is IoU >= tau.

Shifted 90 px right the prediction starts at x = 295 + 90 - 45 = 340, the annotation right edge. Boxes are half-open, so they share no pixel: intersection 0, union 6300 + 6300 - 0 = 12600, IoU = 0 / 12600 = 0. The bound is still 6300 / 6300 = 1.

At lambda 0.5 the prediction is 45 x 35 = 1575 at (273, 258), inside the annotation. Intersection 1575, union 6300 + 1575 - 1575 = 6300, IoU = 1575 / 6300 = 0.25; the bound 1575 / 6300 = 0.25 is below tau = 0.5, so no shift reaches it.

At lambda 2 the prediction is 180 x 140 = 25200 at (205, 205) and contains the annotation: IoU = 6300 / 25200 = 0.25, and the bound 6300 / 25200 = 0.25. With tau = 0.25 the concentric box meets tau exactly, so it counts, and the bound is not below tau.

No defect: box#3 on table#1 against itself. Subject box 90 x 70 unchanged: 6300 / 6300; object box 420 x 110 unchanged: 46200 / 46200. Both IoUs are 1 >= 0.5 and all three names agree, so t-hat ~ t holds and the diff says match.

Subject class box -> glove. Subject box 90 x 70 unchanged: 6300 / 6300; object box 420 x 110 unchanged: 46200 / 46200. Both IoUs are 1, but c(s-hat) = glove != box, so the classification half fails; (glove, on, table) is annotated nowhere in ph-001, so the diff says spurious.

Predicate on -> near. Subject box 90 x 70 unchanged: 6300 / 6300; object box 420 x 110 unchanged: 46200 / 46200. Right place, wrong name: (box, near, table) is annotated nowhere in ph-001, so the diff says spurious, not localization.

Subject box moved 45 px right: it spans x 295 to 385 against 250 to 340, so the overlap is (340 - 295) x 70 = 3150 and the union 6300 + 6300 - 3150 = 9450; IoU = 3150 / 9450 = 0.333 < 0.5. The names agree, so the diff says localization.

Both boxes moved. Subject: 3150 / 9450 = 0.333. Object moved 55 px down: it spans y 355 to 465 against 300 to 410, overlap 420 x (410 - 355) = 23100, union 46200 + 46200 - 23100 = 69300, IoU = 0.333. Names agree: localization.

Predicate on -> near and subject box moved: 3150 / 9450 = 0.333 < 0.5 and a name wrong, so both halves fail. A wrong name is spurious wherever its box sits, so the diff says spurious, as it does for the name alone.
6 objects, 6 x 5 = 30 ordered pairs of distinct objects; the slice has 16 predicates: 30 x 16 = 480, F1's candidate count.
30 ordered pairs, 10 classes for each end, 16 predicates: 30 x 10^2 x 16 = 30 x 100 x 16 = 48,000.
30 ordered pairs and VG-150's 50 predicates (Xu et al. 2017, section 4): 30 x 50 = 1,500, F1's VG-150 count.
30 ordered pairs, VG-150's 150 classes for each end and 50 predicates: 30 x 150^2 x 50 = 30 x 22,500 x 50 = 33,750,000.
